issues.body: The README says adding, renaming, or removing a leg is a two-file change, but immediately broadens that to every issue or PR that "touches a fragment". Later, "When the golden does NOT change" says edits to features, test, tier, tier-reason, or comments are genuinely single-file changes. These rules cannot all be followed. Since this document is expressly meant to define permitted task scope, the broad wording can force unrelated edits to include a shared golden that must remain byte-identical, increasing contention without any required change.
issues.fix_hint: State the rule consistently in terms of changes to the emitted leg-name set: require the fragment and golden only when adding/removing a leg or changing name; explicitly leave non-name field and comment edits as single-file changes. Apply the same qualification to the repeated fragment comments (for example, "a leg-name-set change is a TWO-FILE change") and adjust the documentation-presence test wording accordingly.
issues.title: Two-file scope rule contradicts its own name-only exception

verdict.summary: The added exact-output regression test is non-vacuous and correctly restores sys.argv, and the change does not alter feature-matrix assembly behavior. However, the new scope contract is internally contradictory in the central README and is repeated too broadly across every fragment. It first correctly limits the two-file requirement to adding, renaming, or removing a leg, but then says any PR that merely touches a fragment must include the golden, while a later section correctly says features/test/tier/comment-only edits are single-file changes. Because this documentation is intended to control task decomposition, the contradiction makes the change incomplete and can cause needless shared-golden scope and conflicts.
